command_template: python3 tools/debian_native_container_probe.py CLIENT VERIFIED_DEB DEB_SHA256 VERIFIED_SKILL_ZIP SKILL_SHA256 --fixture-mode dns-truncated --container-memory-mib 128 --sample-server-resources
findings: Both native installed-client workflows received exact EGRESS_DNS_FAILURE for the truncated-host call without denied body text; the approved HTTP controls before and after succeeded.
Each fixture log recorded two truncated.test DNS queries and only the two approved /plain HTTP hits.

Both 128 MiB container runs passed clean package install/removal/residue checks and reported no OOM. An initial exploratory pair exposed an omitted bridge allowlist entry; the harness was corrected before these passing replays.
fixture: Route-free controlled DNS and HTTP namespace. For truncated.test A and AAAA, the UDP responder returns one complete question, no answers and TC=1; no TCP DNS listener is configured. Each native client makes approved GET, truncated-host GET, approved recovery GET through the installed server and companion skill.
limitations: No packet capture was retained. The fixture code sets TC=1, but these client logs do not independently establish the DNS response bits or whether the resolver attempted TCP fallback.

This finite A/AAAA case does not establish behavior for arbitrary DNS truncation, DNSSEC, resolver configurations, or all client versions. The server ran in Debian 12 amd64 containers; native CLIs ran on Ubuntu.
Only guarded_fetch traffic in the fixture namespace was observed. Host-client traffic and traffic sent through other tools are outside scope.

This is an experimental package, not a qualified official candidate. Upgrade, other declared platforms, owner self-review and residual-risk acceptance, and independent human review are not established by this replay. The four AI Scraping Defense repositories need separate adversarial evidence.

container_resource_observation.scope: Container cgroup high-water marks include setup and helper processes; not server-only RSS or FD peaks.
